subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should OpenClaw fix #42291 by fail-closed blocking node-host auth login before credentials are written, or by adding explicit gateway-owned credential forwarding?
rationale: Both options prevent wrong-host OAuth writes, but credential forwarding moves sensitive OAuth material across the node-gateway boundary and needs maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Block before provider auth
options.body: Detect non-loopback remote node-host config before starting login, fail with a clear gateway-host instruction, and cover tokenless node configs plus loopback/local cases in tests.

options.title: Forward through a gateway-owned RPC
options.body: Design and review an explicit credential-sync control-plane API with authentication, auditability, and tests for fresh install and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Declare node-host login unsupported
options.body: Document that auth login must run on the gateway host, close or retarget conflicted PRs, and keep recovery guidance in doctor/status surfaces.

recommendation.title: Block before provider auth
recommendation.body: Detect non-loopback remote node-host config before starting login, fail with a clear gateway-host instruction, and cover tokenless node configs plus loopback/local cases in tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the recent auth-store/current-main refactors and maintainer follow-up PR/comment history for this exact issue cluster.
